title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

errors: Antisymmetry needs facts not checked on the page.
(1) A sub-segment is determined by its closure.

(2) Ĩ_{x0,y} ≠ {x0} and Ĩ_{x0,y} ≠ Ĩ when y is interior. Otherwise the mixed cases (one point an endpoint, the other interior) are not covered; the written argument only treats both = x0 or both interior.

The equivalence (ii) ⇔ (ii bis), x ∈ [x0,y] ⇔ y ∈ [x,x1], is not trivial. It requires a Chasles-type subdivision axiom: an interior point y splits Ĩ into Ĩ_{x0,y} ∪ Ĩ_{y,x1}, meeting only in y. This is called 'évident' without proof.
Totality of the order (needed next page for 'x<y' to describe all pairs) is not addressed here.

ideas.what: Recovering a total order with endpoints from a system of segments/intervals with closures and two-point boundaries (betweenness-type axiomatics).
ideas.modern_name: betweenness relations / ordered geometry; interval structures determining a linear order
ideas.where_published: Classical; the 'géométrie des formes' axiomatics is not in Grothendieck's published texts (only programmatic remarks on tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme).

ideas.what: The 1-dimensional 'bisigned' model as a dense bounded linear order, as a step toward an axiomatic tame topology of shapes.
ideas.modern_name: dense linear orders with endpoints; the 1-dimensional case of o-minimality / tame topology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 discusses 'topologie modérée' programmatically, but not this axiomatics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification that a segment structure on a bisigned 1-dimensional model induces a partial (in fact total) order. This is classical betweenness/order axiomatics with no new content. It is of mild historical interest only as part of the 1986 shape-geometry axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: The interpolation 'ou bien x=x0, y=x0' is written above the line, after 'd'ordre'. The sentence reads roughly: '(puisque [x0,x]=[x0,y] [crossed: I_{x0,x}=I_{x0,y}] dit [crossed: x=y]: si les deux sont x et y identiques à x0, ou bien I_{x0,x}=I_{x0,y} d'où en prenant aussi ∂, x=y)'.
Final line likely 'en prenant aussi ∂' (taking boundaries), not 'on pourra aussi'.
In the first case of the definition, the struck-out symbol before '=Ĩ' (case x=x1) is a crossed-out L/𝓛, so the line reads 'L = Ĩ si x = x1'.
